release_requirements: Create one canonical registry covering capabilities, integrations, agents, workflows, Commander Packs, and public product claims.
Use exactly the lifecycle states CATALOGUED, DESIGNED, IMPLEMENTED, UNIT_VERIFIED, INTEGRATION_VERIFIED, CANARY_VERIFIED, ACTIVE, SELLABLE, DEPRECATED, and RETIRED.

Persist capability ID and version, owner, environment, tenant or global scope, dependencies, activation requirements, verification receipts, last verification time, failure state, public-claim eligibility, and rollback or deactivation path.

Persist data classification, record-required evidence, supported scopes, pricing inclusion or add-on eligibility, tenant feature flags and limits, and complete scope/release context on immutable transition evidence.

Fail closed across website, Tutorial, pricing, checkout, proposals, onboarding, integration lists, member application, and sales claims unless the exact claim capability/version is SELLABLE and tenant-eligible where applicable.
Conservatively import current capabilities without elevating catalogued, mocked, inactive, unverified, coming-soon, disabled, or placeholder records.
Expose a typed public-safe and authenticated Product Truth API plus an internal human-readable administrative view with evidence links and explicit activation requirements.

Audit every lifecycle transition, evaluate required dependencies with environment and tenant ownership compatibility, automatically downgrade or disable dependents when required dependency health is lost, prevent direct unaudited status mutation, and detect claim drift without implementing a duplicate content system.
Pass all deterministic, migration, tenant, browser, production, release-controller, and prior-phase regression gates after current-origin/main reconciliation.

Integrate only through protected main, push immediately, deploy the exact accepted main SHA to Vercel frontend and Railway API and worker, apply and independently audit migrations, and run authenticated production readback.

Create and validate the Phase 203 ReleaseManifest, retain Phase 200 as immediate rollback and Phase 198 as deep restore, certify Phase 203 only after exact production verification, and do not activate Phase 204 before certification.
